title: Servicing Academy Q&A: Contract-Age Scaling of Catch-Up Days
content:
**What is being scaled?** A cure payment on Kestrel Auto Finance Retail Installment Contracts also carries a catch-up amount, applied to principal, equal to one day's interest on the principal balance at the contract APR over the tier's day-count basis multiplied by the catch-up days and rounded to the cent. The catch-up days, once every day added to them has been counted, are scaled by the age of the contract in whole months from the contract date to the payment date.

| Contract age on the payment date | Catch-up days |
|---|---|
| at least 24 whole months | multiplied by the mature-contract catch-up factor, 0.5 |
| 12 to 23 whole months | multiplied by the young-contract catch-up factor, 0.75 |
| younger than 12 whole months | kept as they are |

**Are the scaled days rounded to whole days?** No. They are used as they come out; the only rounding is of the catch-up amount, to the cent.

**Where are the boundaries?** Hypothetical contract date 2024-01-20: a payment on 2026-01-20 is 24 whole months and takes 0.5; on 2026-01-19 it is 23 whole months and takes 0.75; on 2025-01-19 it is 11 whole months and the days are kept.

**A worked figure?** Hypothetical: 14 catch-up days on a contract 18 whole months old become 10.5 days; on a principal balance of 14200.00 at 19.59 percent over a 365-day basis that is a catch-up amount of 80.02. On a contract 30 whole months old the same 14 days become 7 days, 53.35.
